text: The National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2017–2022 set a historical target to enhance consumer protection and increase consumers’ financial capabilities. This is a past strategy target, not a statement of current policy.
section_or_page: Executive Summary, printed pp. xi–xii; strategy targets for 2022
review_note: Historical Ministry of Finance strategy; retrieval disabled pending supervisor decision on BoZ-source eligibility.
original_text: Under the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, the Bank of Zambia prioritizes strengthening consumer protection frameworks and increasing financial capabilities to protect consumers against emerging market risks.

text: The Bank of Zambia requirements document sets out application steps and supporting documents for prospective entities seeking designation to operate a payment system.
source_title: Requirements for Designating a Payment System
review_note: Factual summary corrected; applicant/operator audience requires supervisor scope decision; retrieval disabled.
original_text: Applicants intending to conduct payment system business must submit formal applications to the Bank of Zambia detailing their business structure, policies, and risk management frameworks.

text: The document requires payment-system applicants to submit a risk-management framework and anti-money-laundering/counter-terrorism-financing policies; it also requires KYC and client-verification procedures addressing money-laundering and terrorism or proliferation-financing risks.
source_title: Requirements for Designating a Payment System
section_or_page: Requirements document, printed pp.9–10, sections 1.7 and 1.9
review_note: Removed “robust”; summarized requirements from sections 1.7 and 1.9. Audience decision pending; retrieval disabled.
original_text: Payment system applicants must satisfy the Bank of Zambia that they maintain robust Anti-Money Laundering (AML/CFT) and Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures to prevent financial crimes.

text: The Bank of Zambia states that it shall determine a payment-system designation application within 90 days after receiving a duly completed application. The document says an application is complete only after the Bank gives written notice.
source_title: Requirements for Designating a Payment System
review_note: Added condition that an application is complete only after written notice. Audience decision pending; retrieval disabled.
original_text: The Bank of Zambia determines an application for designation of a payment system within a period of ninety days from the date of receipt of a duly completed application.

text: The 2023 National Payment Systems Directives on Electronic Money Issuance state that an e-money institution must resolve a failed local transaction within 48 hours.
source_title: National Payment Systems Directives on Electronic Money Issuance, 2023
review_note: The official directive explicitly supports the 48-hour requirement, but its current legal status is unconfirmed. Confirm it remains in force and is suitable consumer guidance before approval.
original_text: NEW CANDIDATE — found during the official BoZ source-gap search; no original KB passage.

text: The 2023 National Payment Systems Directives on Electronic Money Issuance require e-money institutions to give customers plain-language complaint information, including how to lodge a complaint, maximum resolution time limits, and appeal options.
source_title: National Payment Systems Directives on Electronic Money Issuance, 2023
review_note: The official directive explicitly supports the complaint-information duty, but its current legal status is unconfirmed. Confirm it remains in force and is suitable consumer guidance before approval.
